walkthroughs.body_html:
Religious Experience — a core area of Religious Studies.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

Religious Experience brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with Religious Experience.

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.

mcqs.q: Whose 1902 Gifford Lectures examined mystical experience?
options: William James
Rudolf Otto
Friedrich Schleiermacher
Mircea Eliade

mcqs.q: Which 16th-century Spanish mystic wrote Interior Castle?
options: John of the Cross
Teresa of Avila
Ignatius Loyola
Francisco Suarez

mcqs.q: How did Hume define a miracle?
options: A violation of the laws of nature by a particular volition of the Deity — and he argued evidence for such violations could never outweigh the uniform experience supporting the laws.
Hume believed all miracles in the Bible really happened.
Atonement means Jesus apologised to humans for being born divine.
Hume defined a miracle as something amazing or unexpected.

mcqs.q: What are the main Christian theories of atonement?
options: Jesus was a human who became God after his resurrection.
Atonement means Jesus apologised to humans for being born divine.

Penal substitution (Christ bore the punishment for sin), Christus Victor (Christ defeated evil powers through the cross), ransom theory (Christ paid a price to free humanity), and moral exemplar (Christ's death inspires love). Different traditions emphasise different theories.
All Christians believe Jesus died only to pay God back for sin.

mcqs.q: What do orthodox Christians believe about the nature of Jesus?
options: Jesus was half God and half human.
He is fully God and fully human at the same time (the incarnation) — both natures united in one person, as defined at the Council of Chalcedon.
Hume believed all miracles in the Bible really happened.
Jesus was a human who became God after his resurrection.
